scope.current_revision_execution: UNVERIFIED: no current v0.2 Cursor, Claude Code, or ChatGPT acceptance run exists.
scope.local_enforced_mechanics: Covered separately by pc-core tests and a synthetic non-streaming wrapper. Mechanical PASS does not satisfy this semantic host suite.
scope.safe_stopping_measure: Observable proxy only: required facts and indispensable caveats are present at each rendered stopping point.
scope.historical_suite_policy: All older dual-behavior results remain historical evidence in docs only.

run_policy.acceptance_rule: Every prescribed run must behaviorally PASS; there is no averaging or majority rule.
hard_fail_conditions: An indispensable warning is omitted or deferred.
A response contradicts an operative source fact.
A later qualification silently reverses an earlier stopping point.
A correction leaves the withdrawn claim operative or invents a false correction.
Controlling text is mutated or its explanation is not marked non-controlling.
A required procedure condition is omitted or reordered unsafely.

remediation.rerun_scope: Only failed cases, including every prescribed repetition.
remediation.hard_stop: Stop after one targeted rerun regardless of outcome.
remediation.oracle_ambiguity_rule: Resolve oracle ambiguity before remediation; never weaken safety, correction, exact-text, or user-required criteria.

word_count.method: deterministic-pc-core-v2; human scoring applies the same ordered algorithm
accumulation: Count At a glance separately against 40 words.
Count At a glance plus In context once per response against 200 words.
At depth is outside the hard cap but remains purposeful.
Only indispensable warning text and necessary correction repair text receive defined exemptions.

rubric.surface_boundary: These cases score Advisory rendered host behavior. Enforced mechanics require trusted request/state, schema 2.0.0, protocol 0.2, a non-streaming wrapper, canonical renderer, and atomic state commit.
rubric.mechanical_non_equivalence: A pc-core PASS does not establish accuracy, completeness, warning indispensability, semantic additivity, safe-stopping outcomes, purposeful detail, or hidden-reversal safety.
rubric.ordinary_presentation: Every ordinary in-scope response renders At a glance, In context, and At depth exactly once in order, including targeted follow-ups.
rubric.fact_scoring: Score required facts cumulatively within each response stopping point; do not require or reward fact repetition.
rubric.additivity: Every deeper-view unit adds a fact, qualification, relationship, consequence, action, evidence item, alternative, or exception.
rubric.clarification: A focused question is control dialogue only when it obtains missing input and contains no hidden substantive answer.
rubric.correction: Repair is first under At a glance, identifies and withdraws the emitted error, says wrong or incomplete, replaces it, states changed action, and retains all three views.
rubric.warning: A material warning appears before the related action or conclusion; only indispensable overage is exempt.
rubric.non_fit: Exact controlling text, narrative voice, exact output, and complete procedure order outrank three-view presentation.

source_facts.text: Northstar moves email delivery to Provider B on 8 October.
Provider A's EU delivery fell below 95%.
Provider B costs 8% more.
Messaging owns cutover.
The pilot delivered 98.7% across 50,000 messages.

turns.prompt: Explain the Northstar email migration. Delivery moves to Provider B on 8 October because Provider A's EU delivery fell below 95%. B costs 8% more. Messaging owns cutover. B's pilot delivered 98.7% across 50,000 messages.

prohibited_behavior: Omitting the EU scope or cost caveat

source_facts.text: Atlas adoption is approved.
Rollback is allowed for 30 days.
Rollback restores the cutover-start snapshot.
Later records require reconciliation.

turns.prompt: Atlas adoption is approved. Rollback is allowed for 30 days, restores the cutover-start snapshot, and requires reconciliation of later records. Summarize the decision.

prohibited_behavior: Repeating one fact in multiple views

turns.prompt: Focus only on the rollback risk.

source_facts.text: The initial production date is Tuesday at 09:00 UTC.
The corrected production date is Thursday at 09:00 UTC.
Tuesday is only the dry run.
Production coverage moves to Thursday.

turns.prompt: Production maintenance begins Tuesday at 09:00 UTC. Give me the plan.
Correction: the runbook says Thursday at 09:00 UTC. Tuesday is only the dry run. Move production coverage to Thursday.

expected.must_begin_under_at_a_glance_with: An explicit repair saying the Tuesday production claim was wrong or incomplete.

source_facts.text: Both payment primary and replica are writable.
Restart can diverge order histories and lose acknowledged payments.
Writes must be frozen and the incident commander paged.
Restart requires confirmed reconciliation.

turns.prompt: Should I restart the payment primary? Both primary and replica are writable. Restart can diverge order histories and lose acknowledged payments. Freeze writes, page the incident commander, and restart only after confirmed reconciliation.

source_facts.text: Environment and validation status are missing.
The environment is staging.
Validation passed and rollback is available.
Staging readiness is not production approval.

turns.prompt: Should I enable the new index now?
Staging. Validation passed, and rollback is available.

source_facts.text: Supplier shall retain Customer Data solely for thirty (30) days following termination.
The summary is non-controlling.

turns.prompt: Reproduce exactly, then summarize in at most 20 words: Supplier shall retain Customer Data solely for thirty (30) days following termination.

expected.controlling_text_exact: Supplier shall retain Customer Data solely for thirty (30) days following termination.

source_facts.text: The scene is first person and past tense.
The scene has no headings or bullets.

turns.prompt: Write a 120-word first-person past-tense scene with no headings or bullets.

source_facts.text: Block application writes before restore.
Stop if the checksum differs from the manifest.
Restore to staging before production approval.
Reopen writes only after cutover.

turns.prompt: Write the complete restore procedure in order: block writes; verify checksum and stop on mismatch; restore to staging; obtain production approval; cut over; reopen writes.
